recipes.name: Mountain Apple Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 2 large Granny Smith apples - peeled, cored, and cut into 8 wedges each
1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle caffeinated citrus-flavored soda (such as Mountain Dew®)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Unroll the crescent roll dough, and separate the sheets into individual triangles. Roll each apple wedge into a triangle of dough, and place them into the baking dish, seam sides down.
Mix the melted butter, sugar, and cinnamon in a bowl, and spoon evenly over the dough-wrapped apple slices. Pour the soda over the rolls.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is browned, the apples are cooked through, and the cobbler is bubbling, 45 to 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mountain Apple Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: Refrigerated crescent roll dough is rolled around apple slices, drizzled with butter and sugar, then topped with the surprise ingredient--a can of Mountain Dew®.

review.reviewBody: This was great but I have a few suggestions that I hope will make it better. First, the appels could be cut a bit smaller. Next put about a 1/2 cup of brown suger in a bowl and add to that a teaspoon of cinnamon, about 3 or 4 tablespoons of a amaretto, and a teaspoon of vanilla. Mix them well together, then add the apples to this. Cover them well and let them stay in that a couple of hours before cooking. This is well worth the time, delicious. Next, when you have your butter melted add the suger and cinnamon to the pan and let the mixture melt together a bit. Becomes a smoother blend. Next, where I live Mountain Dew is not available so I used an orange soda and the result was also yummy. I will provide a photo next time I make this as mine looks very different from this one. I hope everyone enjoys these changes.

I had these a couple years ago made with Sprite or 7up, and they were very good ( I don't eat apple pie, cobbler, dumplings etc.. hardly at all) Anyways I attempted to make these, I listened to many of the reviews on here and I still had some problems which I need to add didn't stop them from being consumed lol. This also was my first time making this so maybe it's trial and error I don't know but next time I'm going to remember cause they were good. So I did everything per instructions but I 50/50 ( brown/white) on the sugar. This is where I messed up I think. : I initially had glass 9X13 baking dish but it seemed there would be too many too close together to cook evenly so I split into sperate pans ( 9X9 I think & 8X11. -weird size that normally doesn't get used ever here ) but evenly spaced apart. I tried to portion the soda sugar liquid on evenly, popped in oven and at 30 minutes the tops were done but I still had good amount of liquid left more so on the slightly bigger pan. The bottoms were soggy so I removed all of them and left them sit for few minutes ( they were still hot anyways). Majority of them did harden to point of no soggy bread but 3 or 4 of them I just removed the bottom piece. The very next day between the half of the portion I took home and the half I left at my dad's- Every. Apple Cresent. Was. Gone! I will be definitely trying this again (1 pan this time maybe a little less liquid ) & hiding a few when done. Thanks

I made this as a trial-run for an upcoming social, so basically threw it together without measuring anything. Used just one tube of rolls for just the hubs and me and it was outstanding! 

I lightened it up considerably. I could never use the amount of butter or sugar called for in the original recipe. I melted less than 1/4 c. butter, mixed this with a 1/2 c of. a mixture of brown and white sugar, cinnamon, a pinch of allspice and 1/2 t. vanilla paste. Spooned it over the apple-stuffed rolls (reduced fat). Then scattered sliced Gala apples into the pan....poured some flat ginger ale that was in the fridge over this mixture (maybe 2/3 cup) and baked for 40 minutes....rolls were turning very dark...I think this needs watching. 

It came out perfect and can tell that this won't be around very long. Hubs gave a thumbs-up for taking to the dinner event.

I used 1/3 less mt. dew and put some cinn. and sugar on the cresents or apples before rolling them up. I also added some Ga. pecans to the sugar butter mix. It was so very amazing with butter pecan ice cream and fun to tell people it was made it mt. dew

I followed the suggestions of some reviewers and it was amazing and easy to make! Coated the apples in brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, rum mix and let that sit a couple hours before proceeding. And as many have suggested, used a combo of brown and white sugar rather than straight 1.5 cups white. Used Sprite - thought the whole can might be too soupy but it turned out just fine. I like that they are easy to serve - might make for an office potluck sometime!

These are FANTASTIC and very easy. Tastes more like an apple strudel. The crunchy top adds a great texture to it. I made a mixture of brown Sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice and rolled the apple slices in that first then I did half and half brown sugar and white sugar for the topping.

I just made this with Peaches it's the BEST so easy and quick.
I used cinnamon and sugar for the top. I didn't use the soda I used the butter and sugar and water to make the syrup to pour over the peaches then sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar on top. yumm.

Not a cobbler by any means, but definitely a great apple "dumpling" dessert! I used half butter amount and half the sugar. Spread a little home made apple butter on the inside of each crescent before rolling the apple inside. Baked for 45 minutes. Will be adding this to the MUST HAVES every fall! Thanks for the recipe!
This really tasted very good. I used grapefruit soda and it turned the apples a pretty pink. I also used more apples and cut the apples in small pieces and put the crescent roll dough flat on top.

I made it but used half the amount of butter and sugar the recipe called for and it was perfectly delicious.

This recipe looks an awful lot like Pioneer Woman's Apple Dumplings recipe and was just as good (minus all the sugar and butter). It's a hit at family BBQ's and gatherings and also at work functions.

I baked them for only about 30m and they were well done.I used only a small amount of stevia and no sugar. This is great finger food a party. I'd like more apples in the dessert. I think I'll try more of a cobbler.
Making this again...our church people love it!!!!! I do as a gal suggested and add brown sugar and cinnamon to apples.. don't have amaretto... probably drank it..lol...great recipe and really easy
No, but, I noticed that when I “3x’s” the recipe the amount of required ungredients did not!!!
My family really enjoyed this. I used Sun Kiss soda and added 1/2tsp vanilla. Thanks for posting this.
It is super easy to make and tasty. My husband ate the whole thing in 2 days.
Excellent dessert.Have made it for several years.
Liked this recipe. Made no changes.
easy recipe to follow, I serve it with some vanilla ice cream
